big_idea: We can write our own code to do a task — drawing a shape, walking a path, telling a story.
learning_intention: We are learning to write our own code with sequence and loop.
student_learning_goal: I can write my own code to do a task with sequence and loop.
success_criteria: I can invent a task and write code for it.
I can use sequence and loop in my code.
I can predict what my code will do AND run it to check.
lesson_specific_materials: OPTIONAL: Coda the Coding Robot — if available; otherwise teacher voices both characters in two distinct voices, or substitutes two stuffed animals / paper-bag puppets / pictures on the anchor poster. Activity is unaffected.

OPTIONAL: Looper the Loop Helper — if available; otherwise teacher voices both characters in two distinct voices, or substitutes two stuffed animals / paper-bag puppets / pictures on the anchor poster. Activity is unaffected.
Per-pair code step cards plus loop cards
Lesson 5 capstone tracker — provided in assessment_suite stage

minds_on.hook: Today YOU write code. Pick a project: draw a shape, walk a path, tell a tiny code story. Then we share!
minds_on.teacher_script:
Bring children to the carpet. Coda + Looper. 'Friends — today is YOUR day. We've learned sequence (Lesson 1), loops (Lesson 2), reading code (Lesson 3), altering code (Lesson 4). Now you put it ALL together.'

Show examples of capstone projects:

Project 1: Draw a triangle. Code: Repeat 3: forward, turn right.
Project 2: Walk a square. Code: Repeat 4: forward, turn right.
Project 3: 'Hello' code. Code: smile, wave, smile, wave (no loop). OR: Repeat 2: smile, wave.
Project 4: Walk to the school flag. Code: forward, forward, turn right, forward, forward.

'Pick a project from this list OR invent your own. Use SEQUENCE for the steps. Use a LOOP if you repeat the same step.'

Show the template structure: (a) Project name, (b) Code (steps + loops), (c) Drawing of the result, (d) Prediction.

'Today is YOUR project.'
student_actions: Pick a project to work on.

steps.instruction: Hand out capstone templates. Children pick a project (from list or invent own) and write the code: 4-8 steps minimum, including at least 1 loop.
steps.teacher_prompt: Say to students: 'Use the template. Pick a project. Write the code. Use AT LEAST one loop.'

steps.instruction: Children work for 10-12 minutes. Teacher circulates and prompts: 'What's your project? What's the first step? Where's your loop?'
steps.teacher_prompt: Stop at each child. Check completeness — sequence, loop, prediction.

steps.instruction: Stretch challenge: include 2 loops in the code. Or alter someone else's code to do something new.
steps.teacher_prompt: Say to extending children: 'Add a SECOND loop. Or take a partner's code and ALTER it.'

steps.instruction: Gallery walk: pairs swap templates and execute each other's code on the grid. Verify the prediction.
steps.teacher_prompt: Say to students: 'Swap with your partner. Execute their code on the grid. Did it match the prediction?'

steps.instruction: Whole-class share: 5-6 children share their project aloud. Discuss the variety of projects and the common code patterns.
steps.teacher_prompt: Pick a variety: shapes, paths, stories. Highlight that DIFFERENT projects use the SAME code building blocks (sequence, loop).

differentiation.for_emerging: Provide a starter project: 'Draw a square'. Child writes the code.
differentiation.for_extending: Stretch: invent a project with 8+ steps and 2+ loops.
differentiation.for_ell_or_iep: Provide picture-supported project ideas. Sentence frame: 'My project is ___. My code is ___.'
differentiation.for_movement_learners: Allow them to ACT OUT their code with classmates.

formative_check.what_to_look_for: Three signals: invents a coherent project; writes code with sequence + loop; predicts and verifies the outcome.
formative_check.how_to_record: Tick the capstone tracker per child.

discussion_prompts: What's the most creative project you saw today?
How did your loop make your code shorter?
What's something about coding you'll remember?
Where might you use coding in real life?
consolidation.exit_routine: Each child receives a Junior Coder certificate. Quick whisper: 'My favourite code project was ___'. Coda and Looper say goodbye with a final code execution celebrating the class.

assessment_in_this_lesson.evidence_collected: Project coherence, sequence + loop usage, prediction accuracy.

expanded_walkthrough.title: When the child writes code that's all sequence (no loop) — repairing the loop-omission in capstone projects
expanded_walkthrough.rationale:
The most common Grade-1 trap on the capstone is loop omission: the child writes 5+ sequential steps without using a loop, even when steps repeat. They forget about loops in the heat of project invention.

The walkthrough covers the precise moment when a child has 'right, right, right, right, right' written without a loop.
expanded_walkthrough.setup: Child is working on a capstone. They've written 5 'right' steps in a row. No loop.
expanded_walkthrough.teacher_script:
Crouch beside the child. 'I see 5 'right' steps. Looper would simplify that. How?' Wait. The child remembers Lesson 2: 'Repeat 5: right.' 'YES! Use a LOOP. Same outcome, shorter code.'

Have the child rewrite. Loop replaces the 5 lines.

Now add: 'Always look at your code — do you have repetition? If yes, use a loop. That's Looper's rule.'

Long-term recovery: include a loop check on every code review.
common_misconceptions: Sequence is enough. (Repair: loops save space.)
Loops are for advanced coders. (Repair: loops are for ANY code with repetition.)
Each step needs to be visible. (Repair: a loop body IS the step — just compressed.)
recovery_moves: Always check code for repetition. Spot the pattern.
Use Looper as the 'compress' character. He makes code shorter.
Compare two versions: long sequence vs loop. Visual brevity wins.

parts_outline.task: Code: write 4-8 steps. Use at least 1 loop.
Prediction: draw or describe what the code will do.
Run-and-check: did it match? Why or why not?
